messages:
Tyra (support): FYI customer org-abc seeing intermittent 504s on our /decrypt endpoint since ~04:00 UTC. They reported a bunch of retries and a small billing spike. Says errors started right after a scheduled key alias swap. Can we triage? :eyes:

Raj (sre): Which key alias/region? Any CloudTrail entries for GenerateDataKey/Decrypt?

Tyra (support): aws:kms alias/keys/arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234. Region us-east-1. Customer sent us this error from their SDK: `com.amazonaws.services.kms.model.AWSKMSException: AccessDeniedException: EncryptionContext mismatch` plus occasional `ThrottlingException`/timeouts. They also said CloudTrail for the key shows fewer events around rotation window — possible log gap.

Anne (eng): EncryptionContext mismatch usually means the API call didn't include the same key/value pairs used for encrypt. But the CloudTrail gap is concerning. Could be proxy or header truncation. Any chance their client is hitting a caching layer that strips encctx?

Tyra (support): Customer uses our hosted proxy endpoint (private tenant proxy) then ours calls KMS. They confirmed they pass enc ctx to our proxy. I asked them to paste the base64 of the header but waiting.

Mike (security): Also confirm key is not an HSM custom key where grant constraints differ. If alias swap happened, there could be a short window where grants weren't attached to the new key. Check grant creation logs + key policy.

Raj (sre): I'll run a quick repro against staging with the same alias. Steps I'll try: 1) create a test data blob with client-supplied encctx 2) call our proxy (to emulate customer) 3) inspect outgoing request to KMS.

Anne (eng): Useful snippet to test locally (use aws cli):
```
# create ciphertext
aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/our-test-key --plaintext fileb://payload.bin --encryption-context "CustomerId=org-abc,Env=prod" --region us-east-1 --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > ct.bin
# attempt decrypt without enc ctx (should fail)
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --region us-east-1
# attempt decrypt with enc ctx (should succeed)
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --encryption-context "CustomerId=org-abc,Env=prod" --region us-east-1
```

Raj (sre): I ran a smoke test in staging — decrypt works when we forward the enc ctx. When I hit our proxy with a deliberately long header (1200 chars) the proxy truncates it to 1024 and KMS decrypt fails with EncContext mismatch. Suspect truncation in our nginx/ingress.

Tyra (support): That matches customer: they said some of their encryption-context keys are long JSON blobs.

Mike (security): If truncation is the root cause that's a data integrity / compliance issue (we're changing data on path to KMS). Need an incident classification and notify compliance. Also check CloudTrail gaps — if telemetry didn't capture these calls, that's worse.

Raj (sre): Quick grep: our ingress has `proxy_set_header X-Encryption-Context $http_x_encryption_context;` and nginx default buffer settings can truncate headers >1k. I'll raise a PR to increase `proxy_buffer_size` and `large_client_header_buffers`.

Anne (eng): Also we should avoid relying on a single header. Consider base64 compressing encctx or using POST body to service-to-service rather than a header. For a hotfix, increase header limits and add logging to show outgoing encctx length and MD5 before/after.

Tyra (support): Customer asked for repro steps to show root cause. Can we provide a short runbook they can run against staging? They want proof before we touch prod.

Raj (sre): I'll produce a minimal repro: two curl commands — one that sends an encctx <1k (succeeds) and one >1k (fails). Will include request/response dump.

Mike (security): Parallel action: I need the key policy + grant list for the alias/time range to rule out grant attachment window. Tyra, can you request CloudTrail event IDs/time ranges from customer for when they saw errors?

Tyra (support): On it. Asked them to share request IDs and their SDK logs. Also told them we've opened an internal ticket and will share repro.

sre-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2749 KMS-encctx-truncation-proxy (priority P2). Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-2749

Raj (sre): Next steps for prod mitigation: 1) deploy nginx header size bump behind a canary group 2) enable outgoing encctx md5 logging to CloudWatch for a 6h window 3) add synthetic monitor that sends long encctx to ensure no regression.

Anne (eng): Follow-up: we should add validation on our proxy that rejects encctx > 2k with a clear 4xx so callers get deterministic failure instead of silent KMS mismatch. Also add a note to the dev docs about encctx size limits.

Tyra (support): I'll update the customer with: repro steps, the incident link, and a planned canary for header fix. Asked them if they can temporarily shorten their encctx to work around it. They agreed to try a short-lived mitigation.

Mike (security): I'll review the audit implications and confirm whether we need to notify SOC/compliance. If CloudTrail shows missing entries we'll escalate to infra and AWS account team.

Raj (sre): I'll paste the failing curl repro here in ~10m.

Tyra (support): Thanks everyone, keep me posted and I'll coordinate with the customer for timing. :thumbsup:
